item.title: Kyo-Wagashi: Kyoto's Seasonal Sweets — Guide
item.description: Kyo-wagashi are the refined traditional sweets of Kyoto, developed alongside the tea ceremony and elevated here into an edible art form. Made largely from sweet bean paste, glutinous rice, agar and sugar, they are prized less for sweetness than for beauty: each is shaped and coloured to evoke a season — a pink petal in spring, a cool cube of kingyoku in summer, a russet maple leaf in autumn. Served with a bowl of bitter matcha, a single wagashi is a small ceremony in itself.

item.title: Wagashi Making Class in Kyoto: Shape Your Own Sweets — Guide
item.description: A wagashi-making class is one of the most rewarding hands-on experiences in Kyoto, a direct way into the city’s refined sweet-making tradition. Under the guidance of a confectioner, you learn to shape nerikiri — a smooth, pliable dough of sweet white-bean paste — by hand and with simple tools into the seasonal flowers, leaves and motifs that define kyo-wagashi. It is finer and more meditative work than it looks, demanding a gentle touch, and at the end you sit and eat the two or three sweets you have made with a bowl of matcha.
